title: The flesh is not consubstantial with the Godhead
pass_a_gloss: If anyone says flesh of Christ homoousion i.e. consubstantial with divinity, and does not confess him in form of God and God before ages, emptied himself, took form of servant as written: anathema. How can flesh after time be same-substance with everlasting divinity? Homoousion means same in nature and same everlastingness without change.
pass_b_english: If anyone says that the flesh of Christ is consubstantial with the Godhead, and does not confess that he himself, being in the form of God and God before the ages, emptied himself and took the form of a servant, as it is written (Philippians 2:6-7), let him be anathema.

How can flesh that comes after time be called of the same substance with the everlasting Godhead? That is called consubstantial which is the same in nature, and the same in everlasting duration without change.
source_text: Si quis dicit carnem Christi homoousion, id est consubstantialem esse divinitati, et non confitetur ipsum in forma Dei et Deum esse ante saecula, et seipsum exinanisse, et formam servi accepisse sicut scriptum est, anathema sit. Quomodo autem caro post tempus homoousios, id est eiusdem substantiae, cum sempiterna divinitate dici potest? Homoousion enim dicitur quod est idem natura et eadem sempiternitate invariabiliter.

choices.choice: Keep the Latin column's Greek loanword once, then English consubstantial.
Inline because forma Dei / exinanivit / forma servi is the written kenosis clause.

source_ref: Vossius 1684 Opera omnia, Duodecim Capita de Fide, Cap. II (anathema + interpretatio)
notes_covered: Cap. II anathema against homoousion of flesh with divinity
Explication: post-temporal flesh cannot share the Godhead's everlasting sameness
